raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--log-requests`, both request-log formatters call `redact_watermark_secrets` on every field of the request, and only drop the skipped fields afterwards. Redaction makes a recursive copy of each value, so every logged request copies its whole `input_ids` list. Levels 0 and 1 never print `input_ids`, so that copy is wasted, and the cost grows with prompt length.

## Modifications

The skipped fields are now dropped before redaction, in both `_transform_data_for_logging` and `_dataclass_to_string_truncated`.

The log output stays the same. Redaction treats each field on its own, and the fields that are no longer redacted are the ones that were being dropped anyway.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. This PR only changes the logging path. The benchmark below also checks that the log lines from main and from this PR are identical (same md5, timestamp excluded), and that the watermark key still shows up as `<redacted>`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The benchmark uses `--log-requests-level 1` and logs one received request plus one finished request. The input is a `GenerateReqInput` with a watermark key. CPU only.

| format | `input_ids` length | main (ms) | PR (ms) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| json | 1024 | 2.018 | 0.516 | 3.9x |
| json | 8192 | 12.377 | 0.520 | 23.8x |
| json | 32768 | 47.798 | 0.513 | 93.2x |
| text | 1024 | 1.936 | 0.479 | 4.0x |
| text | 8192 | 12.008 | 0.480 | 25.0x |
| text | 32768 | 46.569 | 0.479 | 97.2x |

Absolute times depend on the machine. The trend does not: on main the cost grows linearly with `input_ids` length, and on this PR it is constant. Levels 2 and 3 skip no fields, so this change does not affect them.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

Run with `python bench_logger.py` on main and on this branch.

```python
# RequestLogger cost vs. input length. Run on main and on this branch.
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import timeit

from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import GenerateReqInput
from sglang.srt.utils.request_logger import RequestLogger


class Capture(logging.Handler):
    def emit(self, record):
        self.line = record.getMessage()


for fmt in ("json", "text"):
    request_logger = RequestLogger(True, 1, fmt, None)
    capture = Capture()
    for target in request_logger.targets:
        target.handlers, target.propagate = [capture], False
    for n in (1024, 8192, 32768):
        req = GenerateReqInput(
            input_ids=list(range(n)),
            sampling_params={"max_new_tokens": 16, "watermark": {"key": "secret"}},
            rid="rid-0",
        )
        out = {
            "text": "x" * 64,
            "output_ids": list(range(256)),
            "meta_info": {"id": "rid-0"},
        }

        def log():
            request_logger.log_received_request(req)
            request_logger.log_finished_request(req, out)

        ms = min(timeit.repeat(log, number=50, repeat=5)) / 50 * 1e3
        line = capture.line
        if fmt == "json":
            line = json.dumps(
                {k: v for k, v in json.loads(line).items() if k != "timestamp"}
            )
        assert "secret" not in line and "<redacted>" in line
        print(
            f"{fmt} input_len={n} ms={ms:.3f} md5={hashlib.md5(line.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]}"
        )
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The tests are in the new file `test/registered/unit/utils/test_request_logger.py`.
  - `test_skipped_fields_are_not_redacted`: with `input_ids` skipped, `redact_watermark_secrets` must receive only `rid` and `sampling_params`. On main it also receives `input_ids`, so this test fails there.
  - `test_redacts_secrets_and_skips_fields` and `test_keeps_all_fields_without_skip_names` check the exact output of both formatters. They pass on main and on this PR, which shows the output is unchanged.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A, no user-facing change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+import dataclasses
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import request_logger
+from sglang.srt.utils.request_logger import (
+    _dataclass_to_string_truncated,
+    _transform_data_for_logging,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class _Req:
+    rid: str
+    input_ids: list
+    sampling_params: dict
+
+
+def _make_req() -> _Req:
+    return _Req(
+        rid="rid-0",
+        input_ids=list(range(8)),
+        sampling_params={"max_new_tokens": 16, "watermark": {"key": "secret"}},
+    )
+
+
+class TestRequestLoggerFormatting(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_redacts_secrets_and_skips_fields(self):
+        req = _make_req()
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _transform_data_for_logging(req, 2048, {"input_ids"}),
+            {
+                "rid": "rid-0",
+                "sampling_params": {
+                    "max_new_tokens": 16,
+                    "watermark": {"key": "<redacted>"},
+                },
+            },
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _dataclass_to_string_truncated(req, 2048, {"input_ids"}),
+            "_Req(rid='rid-0', sampling_params={'max_new_tokens': 16, "
+            "'watermark': {'key': '<redacted>'}})",
+        )
+
+    def test_keeps_all_fields_without_skip_names(self):
+        logged = _transform_data_for_logging(_make_req())
+
+        self.assertEqual(logged["input_ids"], list(range(8)))
+        self.assertEqual(logged["sampling_params"]["watermark"], {"key": "<redacted>"})
+
+    def test_skipped_fields_are_not_redacted(self):
+        for format_fn in (_transform_data_for_logging, _dataclass_to_string_truncated):
+            with (
+                self.subTest(format_fn=format_fn.__name__),
+                patch.object(
+                    request_logger,
+                    "redact_watermark_secrets",
+                    wraps=request_logger.redact_watermark_secrets,
+                ) as redact,
+            ):
+                format_fn(_make_req(), 2048, {"input_ids"})
+
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    set(redact.call_args_list[0].args[0]), {"rid", "sampling_params"}
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
